item.research_question: How can the low-frequency conductivity of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be modeled and predicted?
item.processing_route: DC-magnetron sputtering with a working pressure of 1.5 mTorr and a 40 sccm Ar flow
item.test_conditions: Room temperature, various thicknesses (150 nm to 1200 nm)
key_findings: The conductivity of HEAs can be modulated through the cocktail effect
The plasma frequency and relaxation time are key factors in determining the conductivity of HEAs
The Nb15Mo35Ta15W35 composition exhibits high hardness and excellent conductivity
The conductivity of HEAs tends to differ by an order of magnitude compared to linear combinations of pure elements
The grain size and phase composition have minimal impact on the electrical resistivity of HEAs
item.mechanism: The cocktail effect, lattice distortion, and changes in plasma frequency and relaxation time contribute to the conductivity of HEAs
item.limitations: The study focuses on a specific HEA system and may not be generalizable to other systems
item.future_work: Further investigation of the mechanisms underlying the conductivity of HEAs and exploration of other potential applications
quotes: The cocktail effect on the conductivity of HEA films, defined as the variation of conductivity achieved through linear combination of constituent elements, is exploited and examined
The conductivity of Nb-Mo-Ta-W HEAs can be modulated through the cocktail effect but tends to differ by an order of magnitude compared to linear combinations

records.text: Paper card. Question: How can the low-frequency conductivity of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be modeled and predicted?. System: Nb-Mo-Ta-W HEA system. Processing: DC-magnetron sputtering with a working pressure of 1.5 mTorr and a 40 sccm Ar flow. Test conditions: Room temperature, various thicknesses (150 nm to 1200 nm). Findings: The conductivity of HEAs can be modulated through the cocktail effect; The plasma frequency and relaxation time are key factors in determining the conductivity of HEAs; The Nb15Mo35Ta15W35 composition exhibits high hardness and excellent conductivity; The conductivity of HEAs tends to differ by an order of magnitude compared to linear combinations of pure elements; The grain size and phase composition have minimal impact on the electrical resistivity of HEAs. Mechanism: The cocktail effect, lattice distortion, and changes in plasma frequency and relaxation time contribute to the conductivity of HEAs. Limitations: The study focuses on a specific HEA system and may not be generalizable to other systems. Future work: Further investigation of the mechanisms underlying the conductivity of HEAs and exploration of other potential applications. Quote: "The cocktail effect on the conductivity of HEA films, defined as the variation of conductivity achieved through linear combination of constituent elements, is exploited and examined"
